title: Maryland's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Maryland's 7th Congressional District will determine who represents a heavily Democratic district covering portions of Baltimore City and Baltimore County. Incumbent Democrat Kweisi Mfume, who has served in Congress intermittently since 1987 and returned in a 2020 special election, faces multiple challengers in the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026. The Republican primary field is led by Scott M. Collier, a perennial candidate. Given the district's strong Democratic lean (Cook Political Report: Solid D), the Democratic primary is the de facto decisive contest. Key issues include public safety, economic opportunity, federal workforce impacts, and infrastructure recovery from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The primary is heavily lopsided in favor of the incumbent, and the general election is rated Safe/Solid Democratic by all major forecasters.

candidates.name: Kweisi Mfume
candidates.summary: Kweisi Mfume is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Maryland's 7th Congressional District, first elected in a 2020 special election after previously serving from 1987 to 1996. He is the Ranking Member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations and serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee. Mfume holds a B.A. from Morgan State University and an M.A. from Johns Hopkins University, and has emphasized constituent services, federal funding for Baltimore, and protecting Social Security and Medicare in his campaign.

candidates.name: Mark S. Conway Jr.
candidates.summary: Mark Conway is a Baltimore City Councilmember representing the 4th District, first elected in 2020. He chairs the Public Safety and Government Operations Committee. Conway launched his congressional campaign challenging incumbent Kweisi Mfume in October 2025, positioning himself as a reform-minded alternative focused on public safety accountability, economic development, and government transparency. He did not complete the Baltimore Sun voter guide questionnaire.

candidates.name: Theo R. Gillespie
candidates.summary: Theo Gillespie is a school bus driver and human rights advocate from Baltimore running for Congress as a progressive Democratic candidate. He emphasizes listening to constituents, addressing the cost-of-living crisis, and fighting for LGBTQ+ and transgender rights. Gillespie advocates for auditing defense spending, closing tax loopholes for the wealthy, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.

candidates.name: Scott M. Collier
candidates.summary: Scott Collier is a Republican candidate running for Maryland's 7th Congressional District, previously winning the Republican nomination for this seat in 2022 and 2024. He describes himself as a community advocate and disability advocate who has never accepted campaign contributions. Collier's priorities include crime reduction, education reform, economic improvement, and addressing illegal immigration. He did not complete the Baltimore Sun voter guide questionnaire.
